summary: Hourly usage-window drift caused apparent rate-tier misclassification and provisional credit hold
description:
Issue summary:
NimbleHealth reports an unexpected change in the applied rate tier for a set of hours on the invoice dated 2026-03-09. The invoice line shows a temporary lower per-token rate applied for hours 02:00-04:00 UTC, which later corrected in downstream records. The billing pipeline flagged the discrepancy and placed the invoice into a provisional credit hold while we audit the raw meterings.

Impact:
- Customer sees a confusing invoice line and a provisional credit hold preventing automatic payment routing.
- Risk of incorrect revenue recognition and a customer trust issue if not resolved quickly.
- Affects one dedicated tenant (NimbleHealth) for a 2-hour window only.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity in us-east (prod).
- Model: redwood/pythia-12b-quantized-v2 served from dedicated pool dhp-us-east-3.

Steps to reproduce (high level):
1) Customer ran sustained traffic spike between 02:00-04:30 UTC on 2026-03-08 using pinned model variant.
2) Our metering-batcher aggregate job produced hourly buckets.
3) Billing pipeline applied rate-tier smoothing and generated invoice lines.
4) Downstream anomaly detection identified a mismatch between raw token counts and billed tier, and set invoice to provisional hold.

Observed logs/indicators:
- metering-batcher logs (producer) show job start times at hh:59:30 UTC for affected window (link below).
- Raw token counts from ingestion show consistent totals but split across two buckets instead of a single hour.
- Billing anomaly detector rule: rate-tier-flip threshold triggered at 2026-03-09T07:12:34Z.

Provided artefacts:
- Customer CSV of request IDs and timestamps (uploaded to ticket attachments).
- Relevant log snippets and aggregation timestamps (S3 links in comments).

Customer request:
- Explanation for what caused the apparent rate-tier change.
- Request for provisional credit until audit completes.
- Ask to confirm any long-term risk and remediation plan.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Maya Alvarez (Support): Opened ticket after initial phone call with NimbleHealth billing lead (R. Patel). Customer says their automated payment was blocked by the provisional hold and wants a provisional credit while we investigate.
2026-03-10 - Jordan Fischer (Billing Eng): Acknowledged. Requested raw meter CSV and S3 paths for metering-batcher logs. Assigned SRE to check cron/job timings.

2026-03-10 - Priya Nair (SRE): Note - found metering-batcher executions around 01:59:30 UTC for multiple hosts. Suspect cron expression misinterpretation after a cronlib upgrade deployed 2026-03-07. Collecting full run history for 03-07..03-09.

2026-03-11 - Jordan Fischer (Billing Eng): Cross-checked raw tokens vs billed tokens. Tokens match total counts, but aggregation window boundaries split the spike into two separate hourly buckets which allowed rate-tier algorithm to pick a lower tier for the earlier bucket. Billing pipeline later re-aggregated corrected totals for reports, but initial invoice generation used the split buckets and triggered hold.
2026-03-11 - Customer (R. Patel - NimbleHealth): Accepts provisional credit pending confirmation. Asked for ETA on resolution and whether this will affect their committed reserved capacity billing.

2026-03-12 - Maya Alvarez (Support): Informed customer we will apply provisional credit for the affected invoice line and that we are rolling a fix; follow-up to include the permanent remediation and postmortem.

2026-03-12 - Priya Nair (SRE): Deployment note - reverted cronlib upgrade in canary and pushed a PR to normalize schedule parsing (https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6289). Monitoring running for two cycles; executions now start at hh:00:05 UTC consistently.
investigation_notes: Metering batcher (v1.14.2) started using cronlib v3.2.0 during 2026-03-07 deploy; cronlib changed interpretive behavior for non-zero-second entries. Several hosts started their hourly aggregation at hh:59:30 which split high-throughput windows across two buckets.

Raw ingestion records show total tokens for the 02:00-04:30 window equal to billed usage, confirming no token duplication or data loss; discrepancy is in bucket boundaries used for rate-tier calculation.

Rate-tier smoothing algorithm uses per-hour buckets to determine tier thresholds; when a spike is split, per-hour peak appears lower for an early hour producing a lower temporary tier; later correction re-aggregates but initial invoice generation used the split results.
Billing anomaly detector correctly flagged out-of-band tier change and placed invoice on provisional hold per policy.
resolution: Workaround and fix applied: provisional credit equal to the delta caused by bucket misclassification applied to NimbleHealth's 2026-03-09 invoice (details emailed to customer). Immediate mitigation: reverted cronlib upgrade in canary and pushed schedule normalization patch (PR #6289) to all metering-batcher hosts. Long-term remediation: update CI tests to include cronlib behavior lockfile, add integration tests that simulate high-throughput cross-boundary spikes, and add a billing pipeline re-check that delays final invoice generation by 1 hour if anomaly detector fires during aggregation. Postmortem scheduled and linked (CON-OPS-2026-03-metering-window-drift). Follow-ups: INT-33245 assigned for infra rollout validation and SUP-36321 referenced for related billing smoothing work.
